subject.title: fix: allow trusted host-read html after outbound staging

question: Should OpenClaw accept content-bound SQLite provenance as the trusted host-read lifecycle for generated HTML after outbound staging?
rationale: Automation can verify the code path and tests, but the patch deliberately widens a trusted local HTML boundary and adds persisted security provenance, which needs maintainer/security ownership.

options.title: Accept Content-Bound Provenance
options.body: Accept the sha256/size/realpath SQLite lifecycle and proceed after exact-head rebase and CI because it fixes the message-loss regression without trusting the whole outbound directory.

options.title: Request A Narrower Guard
options.body: Ask the contributor to add a specific extra lifecycle guard, such as bounded TTL pruning or smaller DB-delete batches, before merge.

options.title: Reject This Boundary Expansion
options.body: Close or pause this PR if maintainers prefer not to extend trusted generated HTML beyond the temp root and would rather require a different delivery design.

recommendation.title: Accept Content-Bound Provenance
recommendation.body: Accept the sha256/size/realpath SQLite lifecycle and proceed after exact-head rebase and CI because it fixes the message-loss regression without trusting the whole outbound directory.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the original trusted-generated-HTML seam and has the strongest code-history signal for accepting or changing this trust lifecycle.
